I1.quote: The adsorption of H2 on CG-CMs at 77 K and up to 1 bar was analyzed using a volumetric adsorption analyzer.
I1.location: main, p. 3 (journal p. 236), Section 3.2; gravimetric 298 K measurement also in main, p. 2, Section 2.2

I2.quote: The carbon monoliths were prepared by compressing the mixture of corn grain-based activated carbons and sodium derived carboxymethylcellulose sodium salt.

I3.quote: the maximum hydrogen uptake on three different carbon monoliths was observed in between 2.39–2.45 wt% at 77 K and 1 bar.
I3.location: main, p. 3 (journal p. 236), Section 3.2; also 298 K and 50 bar, main, p. 5, Section 3.3

I4.location: main, p. 3 (journal p. 236), Table 1 (SBET: MR-1/2 2147, MR-1/3 2541, MR-1/4 2647 m2/g, from N2 at 77 K)

I5.quote: The hydrogen (H2) adsorption capacity of the highly porous novel corn grain-based carbon monoliths (CG-CMs) was assessed.

notes: Primary experimental paper. H2 uptake measured at 77 K up to 1 bar (volumetric) and 298 K up to 50 bar (gravimetric, Rubotherm). Monoliths are corn-grain activated carbon plus a carboxymethylcellulose sodium salt binder; carbon taken as the majority component (binder proportion not stated in this paper). Text says 'this is the first report about the adsorption of hydrogen on CG-CMs', so duplicate_data does not apply. Not a review, not retracted (record.json is_retracted false; no retraction notice in text). Text layer and page 3 image checked; Table 1 values match.
